requirement:
`habeas status` MUST group the selected requirement and example judgments marked
FIXME by issue reference and report how many distinct judgments each issue
affects. A recorded FIXME string of the form `owner/repo#N` under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes` MUST identify that issue, compared exactly; any
other string is a gap description without an issue.

A judgment MUST count at most once for each issue, even when that issue occurs
repeatedly or in several FIXME strings. A judgment naming several issues MUST
count in each corresponding group. Judgments with no issue string MUST be counted once in a separate "FIXME without an issue" group.
Issue groups MUST be ordered by decreasing affected-judgment count, then by
reference; the group without an issue MUST follow them. A supplied
selection MUST restrict these counts to the selected subjects.

`--verbose` MUST list the full name and kind of every judgment in each issue
group and in the group without an issue, along with its original FIXME strings.
The summary MUST include valid FIXME determinations even when other evidence
checks fail; grouping MUST NOT hide their validation findings. Malformed
determinations MUST remain validation errors under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.cli.fixme_summary`, so no implementation root is needed. The review roots are empty, and each clause specifies only observable behavior of `habeas status`. I applied the test of whether a different implementation could produce the same output and still satisfy the clause. - **Grouping by issue** ("MUST group the selected requirement and example judgments marked FIXME by issue reference and report how many distinct judgments each issue affects"). This constrains the output. A different grouping data structure, such as a map, a sort-and-fold, or a database query, gives identical output and still conforms. - **Issue identification** ("A recorded FIXME string of the form `owner/repo#N` ... MUST identify that issue, compared exactly"). This is a matching rule on strings. Using a regex, a hand-written parser, or a split gives the same results. The text names no required library or algorithm. - **Counting** ("count at most once for each issue", "count in each corresponding group", and the separate "FIXME without an issue" group). These are counting semantics. Any deduplication mechanism preserves them. - **Ordering** ("decreasing affected-judgment count, then by reference; the group without an issue MUST follow them"). This is the order of the output. Any sort implementation that yields the same order conforms. - **Selection** ("A supplied selection MUST restrict these counts to the selected subjects"). Filtering before or after grouping gives the same counts. - **Verbose output** ("`--verbose` MUST list the full name and kind of every judgment ... along with its original FIXME strings"). This is output content, not a type or signature. - **Validation interplay** ("MUST include valid FIXME determinations even when other evidence checks fail; grouping MUST NOT hide their validation findings. Malformed determinations MUST remain validation errors under `requirements.ci.outcomes`"). These are behavioral outcomes. The text does not say which component validates, or through which named interface. `requirements.ci.outcomes` is cited only as context for the determination format. The text names no required libraries, signatures, types, fields, or delegation through named interfaces. All of its clauses can be checked through behavior, so tests supply the evidence for them. behavioral: Each obligation of `requirements.cli.fixme_summary` maps to a test that asserts its outcome. - **Exact `owner/repo#N` identification.** - `src/fixme.rs#mod[tests]/fn[only_exact_issue_references_identify_issues]` accepts `owner/repo#7`. It rejects a URL, `FIXME(owner/repo#8)`, prose around a reference, a bare `#7` and `owner/repo#007`. The rejected strings land in the "FIXME without an issue" group. - `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_groups_fixme_judgments_by_distinct_exact_issue]` keeps `Rust-Lang/rust#456` and `rust-lang/rust#456` as separate groups. This shows the comparison is exact. It also checks that `#123` and a github.com URL create no group. - The rejection of `owner/repo#007` is not stated by the text. It is an edge case the text does not name, so I don't count it as a gap. - **Count each judgment at most once per issue, and in every issue it names.** `fn[verbose_output_lists_each_judgment_under_every_group_it_belongs_to]` adds `rules.both` with `o/r#1, o/r#2, o/r#1`. It asserts `o/r#1` affects 2 judgments (`rules.both` and `rules.one`), and that `rules.both` also appears under `o/r#2`. - **Separate "FIXME without an issue" group.** The unit tests assert the group's count, its pluralisation and its members. The integration tests assert it appears after the issue groups. They also assert it is the only group when only `rules.unlinked` is selected. - **Ordering.** `fn[groups_order_by_decreasing_count_before_reference]` expects `o/r#9` (3), then `o/r#1` and `o/r#5` (1 each) in reference order. `o/r#9` sorts after `o/r#1` as text, so the test distinguishes count ordering from reference ordering. The integration test checks the same count-then-reference order on real output, and checks the no-issue group comes last. - **Selection restriction.** `fn[verbose_status_lists_fixme_judgments_and_globs_scope_issue_groups]` selects `rules.case` and then `rules.unlinked`. It asserts the other judgments and issue groups are absent and the counts are 1. - **`--verbose` listing.** - The unit test asserts name and kind lines such as `- `rules.both` (requirement)`, and the original strings in `
o/r#1\no/r#2\no/r#1
`. It also asserts the non-verbose render omits the names. - The integration test asserts the kinds and the original strings of the issue-less judgments appear. It also asserts the output is HTML-escaped. - **Valid FIXME still summarised when other checks fail.** `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[fixme_does_not_hide_stale_inputs_or_uncovered_references]` makes an input stale, so the row is `Invalid`. It asserts `example/io#125` and the "outline input changed" finding both appear in the status output. Searching the repository for that string suggests it only appears in the summary. The assertion on the count is weaker than elsewhere, but the inclusion obligation is checked. `fn[valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book]` asserts "affects 1 judgment" for a valid FIXME and that no validation section appears. - **Malformed determinations remain validation errors.** `fn[malformed_fixme_is_invalid_and_reports_the_required_shape]` asserts the error mentions "nonempty array", the row is `Invalid`, and no "affects" summary line is produced. I found no behavioural obligation without a test, and no wrong expected results.

text: :::{req} fixme_summary
`habeas status` MUST group the selected requirement and example judgments marked
FIXME by issue reference and report how many distinct judgments each issue
affects. A recorded FIXME string of the form `owner/repo#N` under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes` MUST identify that issue, compared exactly; any
other string is a gap description without an issue.
A judgment MUST count at most once for each issue, even when that issue occurs
repeatedly or in several FIXME strings. A judgment naming several issues MUST
count in each corresponding group. Judgments with no issue string MUST be counted once in a separate "FIXME without an issue" group.
Issue groups MUST be ordered by decreasing affected-judgment count, then by
reference; the group without an issue MUST follow them. A supplied
selection MUST restrict these counts to the selected subjects.
`--verbose` MUST list the full name and kind of every judgment in each issue
group and in the group without an issue, along with its original FIXME strings.
The summary MUST include valid FIXME determinations even when other evidence
checks fail; grouping MUST NOT hide their validation findings. Malformed
determinations MUST remain validation errors under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.
:::{req} outcomes
Every assessment judgment MUST use one of these outcomes, applying
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`:
- `true`: for a non-distributed requirement, both its structural and behavioral
checks find no gap under {cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review` and
{cite}`requirements.authoring.behavioral_review`, including their conclusions
when an edge kind is absent. Behavioral checks include the applicable testing
exemptions and obligations assessed by a refining requirement or a site's
own review under {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`. For an example, the
reviewed tests adequately check its scenario and expected outcomes under
those criteria. Distributed requirements, citations, and site reviews find
no gap under their own tasks.
- `false`: the sources do not support the subject, or information is missing,
and the gaps are not all acknowledged by `{fixme}` references to it.
- `FIXME`: some aspects remain unmet or untested, and `{fixme}` references to
the subject acknowledge every one of those gaps. The reviewer MUST explain the
gaps and their source locations in the rationale and record their issue
references or other identifying content from the supplied acknowledgments or
inputs.
The JSON `determination` MUST be `true`, `false`, or an object containing exactly
`"FIXME"` with a nonempty array of nonempty strings, such as
`{"FIXME": ["example/queue#125", "rust-lang/rust#123"]}`. A gap MUST count as
acknowledged only by a `{fixme}` reference under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` whose body describes that gap and that
references the assessed definition, or, for a site review, the distributed requirement from within that site; a citation review MUST NOT accept a `{fixme}`; a plain
`FIXME` comment, another marker such as `TODO`, or prose MUST NOT. The strings
MUST list each distinct issue reference the acknowledging `{fixme}` references
name in their option lines, as written after `:github:`, and, for a `{fixme}`
naming no issue, its body's words, without comment delimiters, joined by single
spaces. A `{fixme}` reference describing a gap that the review establishes no
longer exists within its task's scope MUST itself be treated as a gap. A reference
describing only an implementation defect MUST NOT create a test-adequacy gap or
require implementation review; it MUST acknowledge a testing gap only when its
body describes that same gap. A `{fixme}` naming a GitHub issue that
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads` reports closed MUST NOT count as
acknowledging its gap. A FIXME judgment MUST be grounded in recorded evidence
inputs or, for an acknowledgment supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`, the reference-set digest covering
that acknowledgment.
